column3: Power engineers and power systems operators
column5: This group performs some or all of the following duties:

column3: Power engineers and power systems operators
Power engineers and power systems operators
column5: Operate automated or computerized control systems, stationary engines and auxiliary equipment such as reactors, boilers, turbines, generators, pumps, compressors, pollution control devices and other equipment to generate electrical power and to provide light, heat, ventilation and refrigeration for buildings and industrial plants and facilities

column3: Power engineers and power systems operators
column5: Start up and shut down power plant equipment, control switching operations, control water levels and communicate with systems operators to regulate and co-ordinate transmission loads, frequency and line voltages

column3: Power engineers and power systems operators
column5: Monitor and inspect plant equipment, computer terminals, switches, valves, gauges, alarms, meters and other instruments to measure temperature, pressure, air and fuel flow and emissions to detect leaks or other equipment malfunctions and to ensure plant equipment is operating at maximum efficiency

column3: Power engineers and power systems operators
column5: Analyze and record instrument readings and equipment malfunctions

column3: Power engineers and power systems operators
column5: Troubleshoot and perform corrective action and minor repairs to prevent equipment or system failure

column3: Power engineers and power systems operators
column5: Respond to emergency situations if required

column3: Power engineers and power systems operators
column5: Clean and lubricate generators, turbines, pumps and compressors and perform other routine equipment maintenance duties using appropriate lubricants and hand, power and precision tools

column3: Power engineers and power systems operators
column5: Maintain a daily log of operation, maintenance and safety activities, and write reports on plant operation and non-compliance

column3: Power engineers and power systems operators
column5: May assist in the development of operation, maintenance and safety procedures.

column3: Power engineers and power systems operators
Power engineers and power systems operators
column5: Operate and monitor computerized switchboards and auxiliary equipment in electrical control centres to control the distribution and to regulate the flow of electrical power in the transmission network

column3: Power engineers and power systems operators
column5: Co-ordinate, schedule and direct generating station and substation power loads and line voltages to meet distribution demands during daily operations, system outages, repairs and importing or exporting of power

column3: Power engineers and power systems operators
column5: Monitor and visually inspect station instruments, meters and alarms to ensure transmission voltages and line loadings are within prescribed limits and to detect equipment failure, line disturbances and outages

column3: Power engineers and power systems operators
column5: Issue work and test permits to electrical and mechanical maintenance personnel, assist maintenance and technical personnel to locate and isolate system problems, and assist during routine system testing

column3: Power engineers and power systems operators
column5: Complete and maintain station records, logs and reports.

column3: Power engineers and power systems operators
column5: Completion of secondary school is usually required.

column3: Power engineers and power systems operators
column5: Power engineers require a college training program in power engineering and several years of work experience.

column3: Power engineers and power systems operators
column5: Power engineers require a provincial or territorial power engineering certificate according to class.

column3: Power engineers and power systems operators
column5: Stationary engineer trade certification according to class is compulsory in Nova Scotia and Quebec and available, but voluntary in New Brunswick.

column3: Power engineers and power systems operators
column5: Power systems operators require completion of a three- to five-year power system operator apprenticeship program  or Over three years of work experience in the trade and some college or industry courses in electrical and electronic technology.

column3: Power engineers and power systems operators
column5: Trade certification is available, but voluntary for power systems operators in Newfoundland and Labrador.

column3: Power engineers and power systems operators
column5: Control room operators at nuclear power plants require licensing from the Canadian Nuclear Safety Commission.

column3: Power engineers and power systems operators
column5: There is little mobility between nuclear power generation station operators and other classic or alternative power generation station operators.

column3: Power engineers and power systems operators
column5: Progression from lower to higher classes for power or stationary engineers is dependent on further training and experience.

column3: Power engineers and power systems operators
column5: Progression to supervisory positions is possible with experience.

column3: Water and waste treatment plant operators
column5: This group performs some or all of the following duties:

column3: Water and waste treatment plant operators
Water and waste treatment plant operators
column5: Operate and monitor computerized control systems and related equipment in water filtration and treatment plants to regulate the treatment and distribution of water

column3: Water and waste treatment plant operators
column5: Monitor and inspect plant equipment and systems to detect equipment malfunctions and to ensure plant systems are operating normally

column3: Water and waste treatment plant operators
column5: Read flow meters, gauges and other recording instruments to measure water output and consumption levels, bacterial content, chlorine and fluoride levels

column3: Water and waste treatment plant operators
column5: Collect and test water samples for chemical and bacterial content, analyze test results and instrument readings and make adjustments to plant equipment and systems to ensure quality control

column3: Water and waste treatment plant operators
column5: Provide verbal or written instructions for process control changes to waterworks system to ensure water produced meets standardized quality requirements

column3: Water and waste treatment plant operators
column5: Perform security checks in plant and on grounds

column3: Water and waste treatment plant operators
column5: Respond to public enquiries regarding water quality issues and emergencies

column3: Water and waste treatment plant operators
column5: Complete and maintain plant logs, reports and statistics

column3: Water and waste treatment plant operators
column5: May perform minor maintenance or assist skilled tradespersons with installation and repair of plant machinery

column3: Water and waste treatment plant operators
column5: May measure, mix and transport chemicals to maintain feed stocks.

column3: Water and waste treatment plant operators
Water and waste treatment plant operators
column5: Operate and monitor computerized control systems and related equipment in wastewater treatment, sewage treatment and liquid waste plants to regulate the flow of sewage through settling, aeration and digestion tanks, and to treat and dispose of sewage and wastes

column3: Water and waste treatment plant operators
column5: Patrol plant to check pumps, motors, filters, chlorinators and other plant equipment; monitor and read gauges, meters and other recording instruments to detect equipment malfunctions and ensure plant systems and equipment are operating within prescribed limits

column3: Water and waste treatment plant operators
column5: Test and adjust chemical feed rates to ensure that disinfection processes meet quality standards

column3: Water and waste treatment plant operators
column5: Collect waste and sewage samples, test and analyze results and make adjustments to plant equipment and systems as required

column3: Water and waste treatment plant operators
column5: Perform security checks in plant and on grounds

column3: Water and waste treatment plant operators
column5: Complete and maintain plant logs and reports

column3: Water and waste treatment plant operators
column5: Perform preventive maintenance on plant equipment to ensure that the facility operates in accordance with required standards

column3: Water and waste treatment plant operators
column5: May assist skilled tradespersons with installation and repair of plant machinery.

column3: Water and waste treatment plant operators
column5: Completion of secondary school is required.

column3: Water and waste treatment plant operators
column5: College or industry training courses in chemistry, pollution control or related subjects are usually required.

column3: Water and waste treatment plant operators
column5: Certification in water treatment and distribution (level according to the classification of the plant) is required for water treatment plant operators.

column3: Water and waste treatment plant operators
column5: Drinking water certification is required in Quebec and Ontario for operators whose work involves water treatment and distribution.

column3: Water and waste treatment plant operators
column5: Certification in wastewater collection and wastewater treatment (level according to the classification of the plant) is required for wastewater treatment plant operators.

column3: Water and waste treatment plant operators
column5: Solid waste, landfill or compost facility operator certification may be required for operators in waste treatment plants.

column3: Water and waste treatment plant operators
column5: Certification in workplace hazardous materials information system (WHMIS), transportation of dangerous goods (TDG), and courses in safety practices may be required.

column3: Water and waste treatment plant operators
Water and waste treatment plant operators
column5: Previous experience as a worker in the water treatment or wastewater field may be required.

column3: Water and waste treatment plant operators
column5: There is limited mobility between water treatment plant and waste plant operators.

column3: Water and waste treatment plant operators
column5: Progression to supervisory positions is possible with experience.

This group performs some or all of the following duties:

Make and repair sand moulds using patterns, moulding boxes, sand and hand tools following bench, floor or pit moulding methods; operate ovens to dry moulds; may pour molten metal into moulds to produce metal castings.

Make cores for use inside moulds to form holes or void spaces in castings using core boxes, sand, hammer and wire or other reinforcing material; coat cores with protective materials and bake cores in oven.
Set up, adjust and operate various mouldmaking and coremaking machines to make sand and ceramics moulds and cores.
Set up and operate various casting machines to cast ferrous and non-ferrous metal products; hand ladle and pour molten metal into moulds to produce castings.
Operate furnaces used to melt metals for moulding and casting.
Completion of secondary school may be required.
Up to two years of on-the-job training are required for manual mouldmakers; several months of on-the-job training are required for other workers in this unit group.

This group performs some or all of the following duties:
Operate front-end loaders and stationary deck cranes to feed logs into the sawmill

Examine logs and rough lumber to determine size, condition, quality and other characteristics to decide best lumber cuts to carry out, or use automated equipment to convey logs through laser scanners which determine the most productive and profitable cutting patterns
Operate automated lumbermill from control rooms or consoles to saw logs into rough lumber; saw, trim and plane rough lumber into dressed lumber of various sizes; and saw or split shingles and shakes
Start conveyor system to move logs and lumber to and from saws
Set up and adjust saw equipment and replace blades or bands using wrenches, gauges and other hand tools
Operate equipment to sort and stack lumber by length and thickness, move stacks to storage areas or drying kilns, and feed lumber through planers
Monitor movement of lumber and computer screens to ensure cuts are made according to specifications, and print production reports
Completion of secondary school is usually required.
College courses in wood processing technology may be required.
Several weeks of on-the-job training are usually provided.
Head sawyers and planer operators usually require several years of experience in other sawmill machine operating positions in the same company.
A certificate in industrial first aid may be required.
There is some mobility among jobs in this occupational group.
Progression to supervisory positions is possible with experience.

Operate and tend kilns, treating tanks and other equipment to dry lumber and other wood products, and to treat chemically and impregnate wood products with preservatives
Observe equipment, panel indicators, video monitors, and other instruments to detect malfunctions and ensure that processes are operating according to specifications

Supervisors of woodworking machine operators  (See 9224 Supervisors, furniture and fixtures manufacturing)
This group performs some or all of the following duties:

Set up, program and operate one or more computer numerically controlled (CNC) or manual woodworking machines such as saws, moulders, lathes, routers, planers, edgers, pressing machines, shapers, drills and sanders to fabricate or repair wooden parts for furniture, fixtures and other wood products
Operate gluing machines to glue pieces of wood together or press and affix wood veneer to wood surfaces
Operate preset special-purpose woodworking machines to fabricate wood products such as coat hangers, mop handles, clothes pins and other products
Read and interpret specifications or follow verbal instructions
May clean and lubricate equipment, and replace parts as necessary.
Some secondary school education is usually required.
Experience as a labourer in the same company may be required.
Mobility is common among jobs in this unit group.
Progression to supervisory positions is possible with experience.

column3: Electronics assemblers, fabricators, inspectors and testers

column3: Industrial painters, coaters and metal finishing process operators
column5: This group performs some or all of the following duties:

column3: Industrial painters, coaters and metal finishing process operators
Industrial painters, coaters and metal finishing process operators
column5: Select appropriate paint or mix paints using automated paint mixing equipment according to a predetermined formula

column3: Industrial painters, coaters and metal finishing process operators
column5: Operate or tend equipment to clean, wash, strip, sand, remove corrosion, fill dents or otherwise prepare items for application of paint, lacquer or other protective or decorative coatings

column3: Industrial painters, coaters and metal finishing process operators
column5: Operate or tend automated spray paint, dip or flow coating equipment or other mechanized painting or product coating application equipment

column3: Industrial painters, coaters and metal finishing process operators
column5: Operate hand-held spray guns to spray paint or coat stationary items or items on moving conveyor system with protective or decorative coatings

column3: Industrial painters, coaters and metal finishing process operators
column5: Paint small items and apply touch-ups using paint brushes

column3: Industrial painters, coaters and metal finishing process operators
column5: Clean and maintain painting and coating, ventilation, compressed air and personal protective equipment

column3: Industrial painters, coaters and metal finishing process operators
column5: May prepare and apply stencils, computer-generated decals or other decorative items on finished products.

column3: Industrial painters, coaters and metal finishing process operators
Industrial painters, coaters and metal finishing process operators
column5: Prepare and mix metallizing solutions according to formulas or specifications

column3: Industrial painters, coaters and metal finishing process operators
column5: Operate or tend equipment to clean, degrease, pickle and etch metal and non-metal surfaces to prepare workpieces with desired surface characteristics

column3: Industrial painters, coaters and metal finishing process operators
column5: Tend automatic metal coating machines which convey objects through a series of cleaning, rinsing and plating solutions

column3: Industrial painters, coaters and metal finishing process operators
column5: Operate and control electroplating equipment to coat metal and other workpieces

column3: Industrial painters, coaters and metal finishing process operators
column5: Operate hot-dip metal plating equipment to galvanize metal and other workpieces

column3: Industrial painters, coaters and metal finishing process operators
column5: Operate spray equipment to build up worn or damaged parts or to bond protective or decorative coatings on various objects

column3: Industrial painters, coaters and metal finishing process operators
column5: Check proper thickness of plating using micrometers, calipers or other devices

column3: Industrial painters, coaters and metal finishing process operators
column5: May operate equipment to polish metallic surfaces of products

column3: Industrial painters, coaters and metal finishing process operators
column5: May tend ovens which cure metal coating.

column3: Industrial painters, coaters and metal finishing process operators
column5: Some secondary school education is usually required.

column3: Industrial painters, coaters and metal finishing process operators
column5: Some experience in operating production machinery or equipment may be required.

column3: Industrial painters, coaters and metal finishing process operators
column5: Several months of on-the-job training are usually provided.

column3: Industrial painters, coaters and metal finishing process operators
column5: Some industrial painters, such as aviation painters, may require specialized training and certification or college courses.

column3: Industrial painters, coaters and metal finishing process operators
column5: Progression to supervisory positions is possible with experience.
